name: Budget 18-DOF Tendon Hand (Mahdi)
summary: A 3D-printed, servo-driven robot hand and forearm with 18 degrees of freedom, reported by Hackaday at under $300 in parts. Servos sit in the forearm and pull thin steel-rope tendons routed through PTFE tubes and each joint's centre of rotation; each finger moves side to side and flexes two joints independently. Openness is unconfirmed: the article names no repository or project page, so `research-only` is a placeholder until the design's release terms are found.
